one_line: Paramara king of Malwa waging multi-front campaigns on the Narmada frontier and Konkan in the early 11th century.

appearance.age_look: mid-30s, athletic and broad-shouldered with a disciplined warrior-scholar build
appearance.face: oval face with sharp jawline, medium wheatish-brown complexion, straight well-defined nose, neatly trimmed mustache with a short goatee, intense almond-shaped eyes with a steady calculating gaze, default expression a calm, composed half-frown that hints at strategic focus
appearance.hair: thick black hair drawn back into a high kshatriya-style topknot at the crown, the rest gathered into a short tied tail; a narrow gold circlet with a small central leaf-shaped ornament sits low on the forehead, and a deep maroon cloth band wraps under it like a turban-strip anchoring the topknot
appearance.costume: era-accurate early-11th-century central Indian kshatriya attire: a long-sleeved, knee-length angarakha-style tunic of finely woven off-white cotton with a subtle diagonal wrap and side-tie under the right arm, worn over a fitted maroon cotton uttariya draped from the left shoulder across the chest and around the back like a sash; below, he wears a deep-indigo cotton dhoti tightly wrapped and pleated, reaching just above the ankles with neat front pleats, secured by a dark brown leather war-belt with a simple rectangular bronze buckle; over the tunic he wears a sleeveless, close-fitting quilted leather and textile jerkin in muted olive-brown, stitched in small diamond patterns for padding over the chest and back, but cut high at the arms for mobility; his forearms are protected by plain bronze bracers strapped over the angarakha, and he has simple bronze anklets above sturdy dark brown leather sandals; jewellery is restrained yet royal—small round gold stud earrings, a single medium-thick gold chain with a tiny leaf-shaped pendant, and a narrow gold armlet on his right upper arm; fabrics are matte, practical, with minimal patterns beyond subtle border lines in maroon and indigo at the edges of the uttariya and dhoti
appearance.signature: a straight, slightly broad-bladed early-medieval Indian sword (similar to a khanda’s precursor) with a gently tapering double-edged blade, simple crossguard and round pommel, carried in a plain dark brown leather scabbard slung from his belt on his left hip, right hand often resting on the hilt in a ready-but-composed stance

ref_desc: Bhoja of Dhara is a mid-30s wheatish warrior-king with a black topknot under a gold circlet and maroon headband, wearing an off-white angarakha, maroon uttariya, indigo dhoti, olive-brown quilted jerkin, bronze bracers, and a leather-belted early Indian sword in a dark brown scabbard.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Bhoja of Dhara as a dignified early-11th-century Paramara king and field commander: a mid-30s, athletic, wheatish-brown man with an oval face, sharp jawline, trimmed mustache and short goatee, and intense almond-shaped eyes in a calm, focused expression. His thick black hair is pulled into a high topknot at the crown with a short tail, secured by a narrow gold circlet with a small central leaf ornament and a deep maroon cloth band wrapped beneath it. Dress him in an off-white, long-sleeved, knee-length angarakha tunic with a diagonal wrap and side tie, over which a deep maroon uttariya sash is draped from his left shoulder across his chest and around his back. Over the tunic add a sleeveless, close-fitting olive-brown quilted jerkin with small diamond stitching over chest and back. He wears a tightly wrapped indigo cotton dhoti reaching just above the ankles, neatly pleated in front, held by a dark brown leather belt with a simple bronze buckle. Show plain bronze bracers on his forearms, simple bronze anklets, sturdy dark brown leather sandals, small round gold earrings, a single gold necklace with a tiny leaf pendant, and a narrow gold armlet on his right upper arm. His signature weapon is a straight early-medieval Indian sword with a gently tapering double-edged blade, simple crossguard and round pommel, in a plain dark brown leather scabbard hanging from his belt at the left hip, his right hand often resting on the hilt. Use off-white for the tunic, deep maroon for the sash and headband, indigo for the dhoti, olive-brown for the jerkin, and dark brown for leather, and pose him in a neutral stance with front, side, and three-quarter views highlighting consistent face, hair, costume details, and sword.
